Introduction

Oregon licenses In-Home Care Agencies to provide non-medical personal care services. The OR Health Authority (OHA) — Health Care Regulation & Quality Improvement oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Oregon’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Oregon’s Regulations

OHA licenses in-home care agencies under Oregon Administrative Rules. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the OR Secretary of State, apply for in-home care agency license through OHA, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Oregon benchmarks: Private pay rates $24-$34/hour, Medicaid rates $18-$25/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

Oregon requires background checks and training for all caregivers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting OHA requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Portland, Eugene, Salem, and surrounding communities.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How long does licensing take? Typically 60-90 days.
